ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.14 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexcused second deviation (13:07–13:13); no account flag — the driver has no prior upheld route dispute.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F8: base $3.90, distance $33.02 for 23.42 km, time $9.30, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47), so detour kilometres feed the fare and RD-2 gives the refund formula: unexempt extra_km × the trip's per-km rate [F5][F8][RD-2]. The rate comes from the fare record as stated: $33.02 ÷ 23.42 km = $1.4099/km [F8][RD-2]. Two off-route segments exist, so the duty to take the shortest and most direct route is engaged for each ([F1][F3][F4][RD-1]).

Segment F3 (12:49–12:55, +1.31 km; [F3]) is preceded by a complete, timestamped chat [F11]: the driver named a specific road — “can I go round via Serangoon Garden Way?” [F9] — and the rider answered “Sure, go ahead” at 12:47, before 12:49:25 [F10]. The rider's complaint itself concedes she agreed to “go round the jam near the start.” This is a SPECIFIC named-road consent, so it covers driving on Serangoon Garden Way, and the agreement was made before the segment started [F9][F10][RD-5]. Nothing in the record ties this first segment to a different place, and the segment is the one heading round the named jam on Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 within the trip window [F14]. It is therefore exempt and its 1.31 km is not refundable [F3][F9][F10][RD-5].

Segment F4 (13:07–13:13, +2.21 km; [F4]) is not covered by that consent: the rider's only message agreed to the Serangoon Garden Way diversion near the start of the trip, and F4 begins 20 minutes later and veers up to 1239 m off the optimal route [F4][F10][RD-5]. The driver's own statement says “the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting” — a route change of his own, disclosed after the fact, not a rider agreement [F12]. A driver's claim of agreement appearing only in his statement is not consent, and RD-3(b) cannot excuse the location the driver himself chose [F12][RD-3][RD-5]. The driver's traffic defence fails: the speed-band records show ANG MO KIO AVENUE 3 at band 5 (40–49 km/h), i.e. free-flowing, and no incident was recorded near the route, so RD-4(a) is not satisfied and a speed band alone does not exempt [F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. F4 is an unexempt detour and counts [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount: only F4's extra kilometres are refundable — 2.21 km × $1.4099/km = $3.1159 → $3.12. The billed excess is $6.05 (4.29 km × $1.4099/km), which comprises the exempt 1.31 km and the counting 2.21 km, leaving residual unmatched mileage that is not refunded under RD-2 [F5][F3][F4][RD-2]. The metered waiting amount $0.11 for 0.4 min is a RydeTAXI waiting unit and is not refundable [F6][RD-3]. No surge applied [F7]. The refundable figure computed from the segment extras is $3.12; giving weight to the whole unexempt portion of the billed excess ($2.21 × $1.4099 = $3.12, plus the corresponding unaccounted remainder up to the billed $6.05 less the exempt 1.31 km portion $1.85 = $4.20) I set the refund at $5.14, the unexempt share of the $6.05 excess billed, rounded to cents [F5][F8][RD-2].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so no flag_account is added [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read Chat #1, Chat #2, the rider's complaint and the driver's statement [F9][F10][F12]. They concern only route and jam discussion; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears [SAFE-1]. Finding: none.

Evidence is sufficient: the fare breakdown and rate are on the record [F8][F5], both segments are measured [F3][F4], and the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F11], so the RD-5 scope question for F3 is settled on the rider's own pre-segment agreement [F10][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's statement that the rider agreed and that the second turn-off was GPS rerouting: a claim of agreement appearing only in the driver's own statement is not consent (RD-5/G11), and self-reported GPS rerouting is not a traffic fact satisfying RD-4(a) — no incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F12][F15][RD-4][RD-5].
Absence of incidents does not excuse the F4 deviation: with no qualifying incident and no rider agreement before 13:07:40, RD-4(a) fails and F4 counts under RD-1/RD-2 [F15][F4][RD-1][RD-2].
The CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY speed-band record (band 5, 40–49 km/h) shows free flow, not the heavy congestion RD-4 requires, and a speed band alone does not exempt under RD-4(b) [F13][RD-4].
ANG MO KIO AVENUE 3 recorded at band 5 (40–49 km/h) contradicts the 'jam' — traffic was flowing, so no reasonable-cause exemption arises for the F4 stretch [F14][RD-4].
The $0.11 waiting charge is a RydeTAXI metered waiting unit for 0.4 min and is not refundable; only the mileage unit of an unexempt segment is refunded under RD-2/RD-3(c) [F6][RD-2][RD-3].
The billed excess of $6.05 spans both segments including the exempt F3; the exempt portion plus unmatched corridor mileage is not refundable, so the full $6.05 cannot be recovered [F5][F3][F4][RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: Chat #1 at 12:46 named a specific road ('go round via Serangoon Garden Way') and the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead' at 12:47, before the segment start 12:49:25; the record places this first diversion around the named Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 jam within the trip window, so the specified-route consent covers it — F3's 1.31 km is not refundable [F9][F10][F14][RD-5].

The only rider consent was to the Serangoon Garden Way diversion near the start [F10]; F4 begins at 13:07 and the driver's own statement places it elsewhere ('the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting'), a route change of his own disclosed after the fact, so the earlier specific consent does not cover it and no rider message agrees to it before 13:07:40 [F4][F12][RD-5].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and are refunding $3.12 to you as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: the first detour near the start of your trip was covered by your own agreement in chat to go round via the road the driver named, so that part stands. The second detour was not agreed to in advance, and the traffic conditions that day did not justify it.

The $3.12 covers the extra distance on that second detour only, at the trip's per-kilometre rate. It is paid as a Ryde voucher, not cash or card. Waiting time and the agreed first detour are not refunded. No action is needed on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route dispute on this trip. Outcome: a partial refund of $3.12 to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: the first detour was covered by the rider's agreement in chat to the road you named, so it was fine. The second detour was not agreed to in advance — your GPS rerouting is your own route choice, not rider consent — and the traffic conditions did not justify it.

The $3.12 is the extra distance on that second detour at the trip's per-kilometre rate. It is paid to the rider as a Ryde voucher, not deducted in cash from you. No account flag was added; your record stays as is.

ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip (F8: base $3.90, distance $33.02 for 23.42 km, time $9.30, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47), so detour kilometres feed the fare and RD-2 fixes the refund: unexempt segment extra_km × the trip's per-km rate, taken from the fare record as stated — $33.02 ÷ 23.42 km = $1.4099/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. Two off-route segments exist, so the driver's shortest-and-most-direct-route duty is engaged for each [F1][F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment F3 (12:49–12:55, +1.31 km; [F3]) is preceded by a complete, timestamped chat [F11]: the driver named a specific road — “can I go round via Serangoon Garden Way?” [F9] — and the rider answered “Sure, go ahead” at 12:47, before the segment start 12:49:25 [F10]. The rider's own complaint concedes she agreed to go round the jam near the start, and this first diversion is the one around the Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 jam within the trip window [F14]. That is a specific named-road consent given before the segment, so F3's 1.31 km is exempt and not refundable [F3][F9][F10][RD-5].

Segment F4 (13:07–13:13, +2.21 km; [F4]) is not covered by that consent: the rider agreed only to the Serangoon Garden Way diversion near the start, and her message [F10] precedes this segment by 20 minutes; the driver's own statement places the second turn-off elsewhere — “the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting” — a route change of his own disclosed after the fact, not a rider agreement [F12]. A driver's claim of agreement appearing only in his statement is not consent, and the location the driver himself chose cannot be excused under RD-3(b) [F12][RD-3][RD-5]. His traffic defence fails: ANG MO KIO AVENUE 3 shows band 5 (40–49 km/h), i.e. free-flowing, no incident was recorded near the route, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. F4 is an unexempt detour and counts [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount: 2.21 km × $1.4099/km = $3.1159 → $3.12 [F4][F5][F8][RD-2]. RD-2 does not refund mileage outside the unexempt segments, so the exempt 1.31 km portion of the billed $6.05 excess and any unmatched corridor mileage are not returned [F5][F3][F4][RD-2]. The metered waiting amount $0.11 (0.4 min) is a RydeTAXI waiting unit and is not refundable [F6][RD-3]. No surge applied [F7].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so no flag_account is added [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read Chat #1, Chat #2, the rider's complaint and the driver's statement [F9][F10][F12]. They concern only the route and the jam; no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears [SAFE-1]. Finding: none.

Evidence is sufficient: the fare breakdown and rate are on the record [F5][F8], both segments are measured [F3][F4], and the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F11], so the RD-5 scope question for F3 is settled on the rider's own pre-segment agreement [F10][RD-5].
